If the sentence is correct as it is given then choose option E ‘No Correction required’ as the answer.

No information has been receiving on the subject of this question, but inquiry is now being made.
questions.explanation:
The underlined phrase "has been receiving on" is incorrect because:

  • "Has been receiving" (present perfect continuous) suggests an ongoing action, but we need a passive structure.
  • The correct construction should be "has been received", as it correctly conveys that no information has arrived.

Option Analysis:

  • A. has received on: (Incorrect – "has received" requires a subject that can actively receive something, but "information" is passive and requires "has been received")
  • B. were received on: (Incorrect – "were" is plural, but "information" is singular)
  • C. had been received on: (Incorrect – "had been received" suggests past perfect, which is unnecessary here since there is no reference to another past action)
  • D. has been received on: (Correct – "has been received" correctly uses the present perfect passive form, which fits the context)

Correct answer: D. has been received on

The corrected sentence: "No information has been received on the subject of this question, but inquiry is now being made."

questions.question:
Directions: In the question given below, there is a sentence in which one part is given in bold. The part given in bold may or may not be grammatically correct. Choose the best alternative among the four given options, which can replace the part in bold to make the sentence grammatically correct. If the part given in the replacement is correct then choose Option (e) i.e., No Replacement required’ as the answer.

The crops are dying, it must not had rained.
questions.explanation:
The phrase "must not had" is grammatically incorrect. When expressing a deduction or assumption about a past event, we use the structure "must have + past participle." The verb "had" cannot directly follow "must" in this context.
The correct phrase should be "must not have rained", which follows the correct grammatical structure:
 must + not + have + past participle (rained).

This construction is used when we make a logical guess about something that did not happen in the past, based on a present result. In this case, the crops are currently dying, and we are assuming the reason is that it didn’t rain earlier.
Corrected Sentence:
The crops are dying, it must not have rained.

Example:
Incorrect: She is tired. She must not had slept well.
Correct: She is tired. She must not have slept well.
